Native impact/collision announcement source decompilation (DF 53.16 PE)

Scope: read-only static reconstruction of collision, bodily impact, shared damage,
and the directly related finite pronoun/anatomy/name formatting helpers. The
executable was never loaded or executed. This document records native source
operands and control flow. It is not an observation of in-game display.

Images configured in data/runtime/native-pe-images.json:
  Steam/reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
  Classic         PE:6a70b91c:0270a000
Addresses are native virtual addresses at preferred image base 0x140000000.
Function ownership comes from PE exception/unwind metadata (.pdata).

    executable instructions end at 0x1400e9e84, tables follow.

Reconstructed bodily-impact constructor (text-bearing branches)
----------------------------------------------------------------
void bodily_impact(Unit *u, int force) {
  if (force <= 0) return;
  // The physical calculation chooses one or more affected body indexes.
  for each selected body index i {
    if (i already selected) continue;
    name = unit_label(u, flags 1, 1, 1); // call 0x1413b178c
    if (adventure_mode && u == player) owner = "Your";
    else owner = name + "'s";

    // This is inlined here, not the general ordinal body-label helper.
    // u+0x5f8 points to the body-part vector; its element count is
    // (vector.end - vector.begin) / 8. Index i is a signed 16-bit value.
    if (i < 0 || i >= body_parts.size()) {
      body = "body part";
    } else if (body_parts[i].singular_names.empty()) {
      body = "body part";
      if (body_parts[i].count > 1) body += "s";
    } else if (body_parts[i].count > 1) {
      body = body_parts[i].plural_names[0];
    } else {
      body = body_parts[i].singular_names[0];
    }
    // count at part+0x84; singular vector part+0x90..+0x98;
    // plural vector part+0xa8. All names are complete RAW-derived strings.
    prefix = owner + " " + body + " takes the full force of the impact";
    record.kind = 0x12;
    record.flags = 0x20;
    record.text = prefix;
    calculate_damage(u, i, force);
    shared_damage(records, null_attacker, u, null_projectile, damage, context, i);
  }
}

Evidence for quantity/name fallbacks:
  0x1413b1954..0x1413b1976 index validity;
  0x1413b1980..0x1413b199d empty singular-name vector;
  0x1413b19a6..0x1413b19bf count <= 1 selects singular, > 1 plural;
  0x1413b19eb body-part fallback;
  0x1413b1a09..0x1413b1b29 empty-name plural adds literal 's';
  0x1413b1b2d..0x1413b1b4d invalid index assigns singular fallback;
  0x1413b1b6c length 0x23 and 0x1413b1b72 prefix append.
  0x1413b1bd2..0x1413b1beb copies the full prefix into damage record text.
  Steam prefix literal:   0x141784e40, reference 0x1413b1b72.
  Classic prefix literal: 0x14177eab0, reference 0x1413acae2.
There is exactly one impact-prefix verb: "takes". It is still "takes" when the
selected body-name string is plural. No "take" form or owner-free prefix exists
in this native constructor. "Your" and name+"'s" both retain the intervening
space before the body label. The unadorned prefix has no final punctuation.

Shared damage constructor: complete template families
-----------------------------------------------------
Let H denote the complete native damage head. For record.flags & 0x20, H is the
passed record.text, including the entire impact prefix above (see 0xe5a31,
0xe5e74 and repeated branches). Other records build an attack head from typed
actor, attack verb, target, complete anatomical/item target, optional direction,
and optional equipment. Every following family consumes the same H; naming
only the deflection family would omit native alternatives.

Immediate outcome sentences:
  H + ", but it is deflected by " + EQUIPMENT + "!"
  H + ", but the attack is deflected by " + EQUIPMENT + "!"
  H + ", lightly tapping the target!"
  H + ", but there is no force!"
  H + ", but it passes right through!"
  H + ", but the attack passes right through!"
  H + ", but it glances away!"
  H + ", but the attack glances away!"
  H + " and the severed part sails off in an arc!"
  H + " and " + BODY_RESULT + "!"
  H + " and it is mostly cut away from the rest of the torso!"
  H + ", " + DAMAGE_LIST + "!"
  H + " and " + DAMAGE_LIST + "!"
  H + "!"

BODY_RESULT alternatives, complete source bodies (without terminal '!'):
  LAYER + " is smashed into the body, an unrecognizable mass"
  LAYER + " splits in gore"
  LAYER + " collapses"
  LAYER + " is ripped into loose shreds"
  LAYER + " is torn apart"
  LAYER + " is cloven asunder"
  LAYER + " explodes into gore"
  LAYER + " collapses into a lump of gore"
  LAYER + " is crushed"
LAYER uses "the " + full anatomy/tissue/material field, or the native fallback
"the part" / "the injured part". Layer ownership uses full layer + "'s " + name.

DAMAGE alternatives:
  VERB + " the " + LAYER
  "tearing it apart"
  DAMAGE + " through a hole in the " + LAYER
  "passing through a hole in the " + LAYER
  "jamming the " + LAYER + " through the " + LAYER
  "jamming the " + LAYER + " out of the wound"
  "breaking away the " + LAYER
  "breaking away" + FRACTION + " the " + LAYER
VERB: tearing / tearing apart / shattering / chipping / fracturing / denting /
      bruising. Repeated layers joined with " and " may omit repeated verb.
FRACTION: " most of" / " half of" / " a piece of" / " the rest of".
DAMAGE_LIST: ordered DAMAGE elements joined with ", " or " and "; may append
" through the " + EQUIPMENT and/or repeated " and spilling " + FLUID.
FLUID: possessive owner, optional decay adjective, complete RAW material name.
Decay alternatives: rancid / decomposing / rotten / fetid / foul / reeking /
                    filthy / stinking.

Associated injury sentence:
  INJURY_LIST + "!"
INJURY_LIST preserves each injury and joins with ", " or " and ".
INJURY alternatives:
  ARTERY + [" in the " + BODY] + " has been opened by the attack"
  NERVE + [" in the " + BODY] + (" has" | " have") + " been severed"
  "a ligament" + [" in the " + BODY] + " has been " + (torn | sprained | bruised)
  "a tendon" + [" in the " + BODY] + " has been " + (torn | strained | bruised)
ARTERY: a major artery / an artery.
NERVE: many nerves / a motor nerve / a sensory nerve.

Additional shared-damage announcements (full native sentence alternatives):
  "The geldables have been torn away!"
  "It is a gelding strike!"
  "It is a gelding blow!"
  EQUIPMENT + " is ripped to shreds!"
  EQUIPMENT + " breaks!"
  OWNER + " attack is interrupted!"
  UNIT + (" have" | " has") + " become enraged!"
  "The " + ITEM + " has lodged firmly in the wound!"
  UNIT + (" latch on firmly!" | " latches on firmly!")
  UNIT + (" latch on firmly" | " latches on firmly") + " to " + OWNED_OBJECT + "!"
  UNIT + (" are" | " is") + " propelled away by the force of the blow!"
  UNIT + (" have" | " has") + " been knocked unconscious!"
  UNIT + (" have" | " has") + (" been stunned again!" | " been stunned!")
  UNIT + (" are" | " is") +
       (" having more trouble breathing!" | " having trouble breathing!")
  UNIT + (" feel" | " looks") + (" even more sick!" | " sick!")
  FLUID + " is injected into the " + BODY + "!"
  FLUID + (" pours over the " | " flows over the " | " splatters over the " |
           " crumbles over the ") + BODY + "!"
  FLUID + " is sucked out of the wound!"
The aux-event switch subtracts 6 from the record kind, dispatches values 0..28
through 0x1400e9ecc; the decoded table is appended below.

Collision producer: all local complete sentence templates
---------------------------------------------------------
  UNIT + (" skip" | " skips") + " across the " + (water | magma | lava) + "!"
  UNIT + (" slam" | " slams") + " into an obstacle!"
  UNIT + (" slam" | " slams") + " into an obstacle and " + (blow | blows) + " apart!"
  UNIT + (" slam" | " slams") + " into " + UNIT + "!"
  UNIT + (" scramble" | " scrambles" | " roll" | " rolls" | " jump" | " jumps") +
       " out of " + ("your" | UNIT + "'s") + " flight path!"
Slamming-into-obstacle branches at 0x140eaf64e..0x140eaf67c and
0x140eb38a9..0x140eb38d6 then call the bodily-impact constructor. Other local
collision names and target names come from the complete native unit formatter.

Direct text helper branches
---------------------------
Pronoun 0x140aa4730: male -> he, female -> she, other -> it;
optional capitalization changes the initial letter only (He / She / It).
Possessive pronoun 0x140aa4850: male -> his, female -> her, other -> its;
optional capitalization changes the initial letter only (His / Her / Its).
General body label 0x1413345d0 uses valid body index, requested subpart/name index,
singular/plural selection, optional ordinal prefix, and "body part(s)" fallback.
Its complete disassembly follows, separately from the simpler inlined impact
body selector, so the two grammars are not conflated.
Unit label 0x14132e430 and item label 0x140c65450 delegate complete native names;
materials, role labels, creature names, generated proper names, body/tissue RAW
names and item quality markers remain typed dynamic input strings. Their values
are not finite literals in the collision constructor. They must retain the
existing unit/anatomy/item/material namespaces when translating these templates.

Operand inventory convention
----------------------------
The companion TSV records every printable RIP-relative source operand and
printable inline stores, plus all direct calls in the declared native functions.
Fixed-width loads are bounded to the instruction load width; NUL-terminated
references retain their complete source string. Inline stores are machine
operands and can include bookkeeping constants that happen to be printable;
only the semantic branches above are sentence productions. Jump-table entries
are data, decoded as image-relative target RVAs rather than disassembled as code.
The complete native instruction listings below allow every text reference and
branch to be traced without relying on screenshot fragments.
